title: Planck-Scale Microstructure of an Elastic Vacuum and Its First Optical Constitutive Constant
content: We derive the first optical constitutive constant of an elastic vacuum. From two vacuum inputs — the gravitational recovery coefficient 4πG and a Planck-frequency ground state — and the circulation picture of the photon, the filament cross-section follows at exactly two Planck areas, and its ratio to the contact hemisphere of one vacuum cell fixes χ = 1/π. For a slit, the boundary law then yields a helicity-odd, rigid fringe translation Δx = σfλ²/(2πa²), independent of screen thickness and material, with parameter-free predictions from 405 to 1550 nm; pilot interferometry already excludes the competing completion by 77 standard deviations.
